'''Stefano Buono''' (born 1966) is an Italian [[physicist]], and the chief executive officer (CEO) of [[NewCleo|newcleo]], a startup working in the design of small nuclear reactors, which uses waste from other reactors to power itself, he co-founded in 2021.<ref name="2-73-forbes.it-cit">{{cite web|url=https://forbes.it/2023/10/12/newcleo-startup-italiana-nucleare-raccolto-400-milioni/|title=newcleo, la startup italiana del nucleare che ha raccolto 400 milioni}}</ref>

==Biography==
Stefano Buono was born in 1966 in [[Avellino]], Italy. He attended high school in Turin, Italy and received his master's degree in physics from the [[University of Turin]] in 1991.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.adacap.com/company_staff.php?c=00003&a=00011&l=ita|title=Advanced Accelerator Applications - AAA|author=Sviluppo: ITSPlanet S.r.l.|publisher=Adacap.com|accessdate=18 December 2014}}</ref>

==Career as physicist==
Prior to founding Advanced Accelerator Applications in 2002, Buono worked at the Centre for Advanced Studies, Research and Development or [[CRS4]]. During his six years within CRS4, he headed a team of engineers working on different international research projects in the field of energy production and nuclear waste transmutation ([[Accelerator-Driven System]]s). 
Before joining CRS4 and in parallel to his appointment at CRS4,  Buono worked for approximately ten years with physics Nobel laureate [[Carlo Rubbia]] at CERN, one of the leading research laboratories for [[particle physics]] in the world. During that term, he also actively participated in the development of CERN's Adiabatic Resonance Crossing method.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://investing.businessweek.com/research/stocks/private/person.asp?personId=53471831&privcapId=52807520|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141218172433/http://investing.businessweek.com/research/stocks/private/person.asp?personId=53471831&privcapId=52807520|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 18, 2014|title=Stefano Buono: Executive Profile & Biography - Businessweek|work=Businessweek.com|accessdate=18 December 2014}}</ref>

==Advanced Accelerator Applications, Elysia Capital, Planet Smart City, LIFTT==
In 2002, Buono founded [[Advanced Accelerator Applications]] (NASDAQ: AAAP), a radiopharmaceutical company that develops, produces and commercializes molecular [[nuclear medicine]], diagnostic and therapeutic products.<ref>[http://www.dicardiology.com/article/advanced-accelerator-applications-acquires-ge-healthcare’s-fdg-pet-radiopharmaceutical-busin  "Advanced Accelerator Applications Acquires GE Healthcare’s FDG-PET Radiopharmaceutical Business in Italy", Diagnostic and Interventional cardiology, September 2014]</ref> AAA traded on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker “AAAP.” The first day of trading was 11 November 2015. On January 22, 2018, Novartis AG acquired AAA.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Novartis completes tender offer for Advanced Accelerator Applications S.A. and announces commencement of subsequent offering period |url=https://www.novartis.com/news/media-releases/novartis-completes-tender-offer-advanced-accelerator-applications-sa-and-announces-commencement-subsequent-offering-period |access-date=2026-07-27 |website=Novartis |language=en}}</ref>  

Besides being a founder of Advanced Accelerator Applications, Buono has been its CEO and a member of its board of directors until January 2018.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.biospace.com/News/advanced-accelerator-applications-aaa-raises-6-1/297690|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141218181410/http://www.biospace.com/News/advanced-accelerator-applications-aaa-raises-6-1/297690|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 18, 2014|title=Advanced Accelerator Applications AAA|publisher=Biospace|accessdate=18 December 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.molecularimaging.net/topics/molecular-imaging/biomarkers/aaa-acquires-100-share-uk-nuclear-medicine-company|title=AAA acquires 100% share of UK nuclear medicine company|work=Molecular Imaging|accessdate=18 December 2014}}</ref>

In 2018, he founded Elysia Capital, a company based in London and Turin focused on social impact investments in the area of Sustainable Innovation, Wellbeing, Education, Art, and Culture.<ref name="4-31-elysiacapital.com-cit">{{cite web|url=https://www.elysiacapital.com/en/team|title=Elysia Capital}}</ref> He became also Chairman of Planet Smart City, a worldwide leader in integrating smart solutions and social innovation practices in the design and development of large, affordable, smart real estate housing projects.<ref name="5-23-lastampa.it-cit">{{cite web|url=https://www.lastampa.it/torino/2023/05/23/news/planet_smart_city_torino_190_milioni_borsa_nucleare_stefano_buono-12820605/|title=Planet Smart City: così l'impresa torinese ha raccolto 190 milioni - La Stampa}}</ref>

In 2019, Stefano Buono became Chairman of LIFTT, a not-only-profit investment holding focusing on innovation and technology transfer from research institutions.<ref name="6-5-liftt.com-cit">{{cite web|url=https://www.liftt.com/en/about-en/|title=LIFTT - About}}</ref>

==newcleo==

In 2021, he co-founded and incorporated newcleo, a nuclear technology company of which he is CEO.<ref name="2-73-forbes.it-cit"/> Based in UK, Italy, France and Switzerland, the company raised EUR400m reaching in its first year of operation and it currently employs around 700 employees.<ref name="3-59-lastampa.it-cit">{{cite web|url=https://www.lastampa.it/torino/2024/04/20/news/newcleo_nucleare_stefano_buono_cresce_g7-14239966/|title=NewCleo cresce e trasloca, Stefano Buono: "Meeting del nucleare al G7" - La Stampa}}</ref> Its goal is to bring forward the most sustainable strategy for the nuclear industry of the future, with innovations that increase safety, reduce costs, avoid mining, and dramatically reduce nuclear waste. 

He is the author of numerous scientific publications.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://publications.crs4.it/pubdocs/?idAuthor=133&pg=-1|title=Publications de Buono au CRS4|publisher=Publications.crs4.it|accessdate=18 December 2014}}</ref>
